evals.name: edit-saved-address
evals.prompt: Customers can see their saved addresses on /account/addresses but can't edit them. Add editing so they can fix a typo in an address.
evals.expected_output: Each saved address on /account/addresses gets an edit form backed by a server action. The action checks the session itself (middleware.ts only checks that a cookie exists), confirms the address belongs to the signed-in customer before calling PATCH /addresses/{addressId} (docs/backend-api.md says the API does not check ownership and the service token can write any customer's data), validates on the server with the rules of ADR-0004 (six digit PIN not starting with 0, ten digit phone starting 6 to 9, India only) rather than the stale README, and expires the exact per-customer tag the list reads (customer:<id>:addresses). It stays on the fetch-level caching model and the zod 3 API the repository pins (Next 15.5.4, zod 3.25.76), keeps the page a server component with a small client form that imports nothing server-only, leaves the loose read schema able to read old LK addresses, refuses to edit an LK address in place (PATCH never changes country, so the result would still be LK), keeps what the customer typed when a save fails, adds tests for the action (success, invalid input and a failed save, runnable under the repository's vitest config with no real request), adds no dependency and makes no commit. The fixture has no node_modules and the machine has no network, so lint, typecheck, tests and build cannot run here: the grader judges by reading the code, and the run must say what it did not run.
expectations: A customer can edit each saved address from /account/addresses: the page (or a page it links to) renders an edit form per address, prefilled with that address, whose submit saves the change

The save goes through a new function in lib/api.ts (a server-only module) that sends PATCH to /addresses/{addressId} with the Authorization header from the existing call helper, as docs/backend-api.md describes; it is not a PUT, and it is not a request to /customers/{customerId}/addresses/{id}
The form submits to a server action (a function in a "use server" module); no route handler is added for the form to post to or fetch

The action establishes the signed-in customer itself (requireSession() or getSession() with a rejection) before it parses input or calls the API; it does not rely on middleware.ts, which only checks that a sid cookie is present

Before calling PATCH, the action confirms that the submitted address id belongs to the signed-in customer (for example by finding it in listAddresses(session.customerId) or by comparing the customerId of GET /addresses/{addressId}), and refuses otherwise; the customer id comes from the session, never from a form field or hidden input

A test calls the action with an address id that belongs to another customer and asserts it is refused without the PATCH being sent, with the stub at the API boundary (fetch, or the lib/api.ts read returning an address whose customerId differs from the session's); a test that stubs the run's own ownership helper to say "not yours" does not satisfy this, since it would pass with no comparison at all

The action validates the submitted fields on the server with a Zod schema before it sends the PATCH (an ownership lookup may run first; no write happens with unvalidated input): the PIN must be exactly six digits not starting with 0 and the phone ten digits starting with 6, 7, 8 or 9 (ADR-0004), not the README's free-text postcode of up to 10 characters
The edit cannot save a country other than IN: the form offers no country choice (or only IN), and nothing in the change treats Sri Lanka or LK as a valid delivery country
The run either corrects the README sentence saying the shop ships to India and Sri Lanka with 10 character postcodes, or tells the user in its final message that it contradicts ADR-0004

After a successful save the action calls revalidateTag with the tag listAddresses reads, addressesTag(session.customerId) (the string customer:<id>:addresses); revalidating only "addresses" or customerTag(...) (customer:<id>) does not satisfy this, since tags match exactly

The change uses only APIs available in the pinned versions: no updateTag, no "use cache", cacheLife, cacheTag or cacheComponents (Next 16 features, not in next 15.5.4), and no Zod 4 top-level helpers such as z.flattenError, z.treeifyError or z.prettifyError imported from "zod" (zod is pinned at 3.25.76)
app/account/addresses/page.tsx stays a server component (no "use client"); the interactive form is a separate client component
No client component imports lib/api.ts, lib/env.server.ts or lib/session.ts, no NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable is added, and API_TOKEN is read only on the server

The action returns a state the form renders: field errors next to the fields they belong to and a general message for a 422 or other API failure; it never returns the raw error, a stack or the unfiltered API response body (placing the API's 422 per-field messages on the matching known form fields is acceptable); every input has a label and the submit button is disabled while the save is pending

lib/schemas.ts AddressSchema (the read schema) is not tightened to the ADR-0004 rules, so old LK addresses still load: the existing test 'reads an old LK address from the API' in lib/schemas.test.ts is kept unchanged

New tests cover the action's success path (the PATCH is called for the session's customer and the addresses tag is revalidated), a rejected invalid PIN or phone, and a failed save (an API 422 or other failure) that returns an error state and does not revalidate; the tests can run under the repository's vitest config (test/setup.ts supplies test values for API_TOKEN and SESSION_SECRET), with lib/api.ts mocked or fetch stubbed so no test sends a real request; existing tests are not deleted or weakened

When a save fails (a validation error or an API failure), the form still shows what the customer typed, not the address as it was: the error state carries the submitted values back and the form renders them (React 19 resets an uncontrolled form after its action settles, so defaultValue from the saved address alone loses the correction)

An old address whose country is not IN cannot be saved through the edit: PATCH never changes country (docs/backend-api.md), so the action loads the stored address and refuses one whose country is not IN without sending the PATCH, and the page does not offer such an address a form that can only fail (it says the address can no longer be used for delivery, or offers no edit for it)
package.json dependencies and devDependencies are unchanged, middleware.ts and the app/account/profile files are unchanged, and no ADR or decision record is added

The final message says that lint, typecheck, tests and build were not run (no node_modules and no network), or reports their real output if the run managed to run them; it does not claim they pass without running them
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: review-invoice-bulk-actions
evals.prompt: Can you review feat/invoice-bulk-actions before I merge it into main? Finance wants it out this week.
evals.expected_output: A review of the two branch commits against main (nothing edited, nothing committed or merged) that says not to merge as is and ranks the blocking findings first: the ledger service key, which docs/ledger-api.md and .env.example say can read and write every organisation, is shipped to every browser as NEXT_PUBLIC_LEDGER_API_KEY and used with a client-chosen X-Org-Id; bulkDelete trusts an orgId bound with bulkDelete.bind(null, orgId) in the page, but a server action is a public endpoint and any client can call it with another organisation's id; markPaidMany is exported from the "use server" file, so it is itself a callable server action that takes any orgId with no session check at all; Remove hard-deletes issued invoices against ADR-0002; getInvoiceSummary is a "use cache" function that reads the organisation from module state set by the layout, so one organisation's totals reach others. It also finds that bulkMarkPaid's try/catch swallows the redirect requireSession throws, the stale caches (revalidateTag("invoices") matches no tag; the summary tag is never expired), bulkDelete's missing validation, partial batches with no report, the layout's request-time read outside Suspense under cacheComponents and the absent tests, cites file and function for each with a failure scenario and a fix, gives a path for the week's deadline, does not flag the legitimate "use client" files, and says that lint, typecheck, tests and build were not run (no node_modules, no network).
expectations: The run leaves the repository as it found it: no tracked file is modified, no commit is made, feat/invoice-bulk-actions still ends at its fixture commit, main is not changed or merged into, and nothing is pushed
The review's verdict is that the branch should not be merged as it stands, and the blocking findings are listed before the minor ones

Finds that NEXT_PUBLIC_LEDGER_API_KEY (src/env.ts, .env.example, used in exportCsv in bulk-toolbar.tsx) ships the ledger service credential, which reads and writes every organisation's invoices, to every browser together with an X-Org-Id the client supplies; rates it critical or blocking; says the export must run on the server with the session's organisation and the server-only key, and that the key must be rotated if a build with it was ever deployed

Finds that bulkDelete takes orgId as a bound argument (bulkDelete.bind(null, orgId) in src/app/(app)/invoices/page.tsx) and uses it instead of the session's orgId, and explains why binding on the server does not protect it: the action is a public endpoint, so any signed-in user can invoke it with another organisation's id (and the ledger trusts X-Org-Id); rates it critical or blocking and says to read session.orgId inside the action. Accepting the bind as safe because it happens in a server component fails this

Finds that markPaidMany(orgId, ids) is exported from the "use server" module src/features/invoices/actions.ts, which makes it a server action any client can call directly with any orgId and ids, with no requireSession at all (not even a signed-in user is needed); rates it critical or blocking and says to stop exporting it or move it to a server-only module

Finds that bulkMarkPaid calls requireSession() inside a try whose catch returns an error state, so the redirect requireSession throws for a signed-out or expired session is swallowed and the user sees "Could not mark the invoices paid" instead of being sent to /login; says to call it outside the try (or rethrow with unstable_rethrow)

Finds that Remove calls DELETE /invoices/{id} for invoices of any status, contrary to ADR-0002 (issued invoices are voided, only drafts may be deleted), and says Remove must void issued invoices or be limited to drafts

Finds that getInvoiceSummary is a "use cache" function that takes no organisation argument and reads it from the module-level currentOrgId in src/lib/current-org.ts, so the cache entry and the variable are shared across organisations and concurrent requests (one organisation's totals shown to another); says to pass orgId as an argument and tag per organisation

Finds both stale caches: revalidateTag("invoices") in bulkDelete matches no entry because listInvoices is tagged invoices:<orgId>, and no action expires the invoice-summary tag, so the list stays stale after a removal and the totals stay stale after invoices are paid or removed

Finds that a failure part way through a batch is not reported: bulkDelete stops at the first ledger error and throws out of the action, and markPaidMany's Promise.all rejects after some invoices were already marked paid (bulkMarkPaid then reports a generic failure, inviting a retry that records payments twice); says to settle each item and return which succeeded and which failed
Finds that bulkDelete does not validate ids (no Zod parse, no id format, no maximum count, unlike bulkMarkPaid), so arbitrary strings reach the ledger path

Finds that src/app/(app)/layout.tsx now awaits requireSession() (cookies) at the top of the layout with cacheComponents: true in next.config.ts, a request-time read outside any Suspense boundary that breaks the prerendered shell or fails next build
Notes that the branch adds no tests for bulkMarkPaid, bulkDelete or markPaidMany, in particular none proving an action cannot act on another organisation

Answers the deadline: says what must change before anything merges and gives a concrete path for this week, either the whole branch once the named fixes are made or a smaller part first (for example Mark paid once its defects are fixed, with Remove and Export held back); an answer about the whole branch is enough, but only listing defects, or saying it cannot ship this week with no path, fails

Every blocking finding (each one the review says must be fixed before merge) names the file and the function it is about and gives a concrete failure scenario, not only a rule name; minor notes may be brief; any line number the review cites points at the code it describes (a citation past the end of the file, or at unrelated code, fails)

Does not report the "use client" directive in bulk-toolbar.tsx or void-button.tsx as a problem (both use hooks and event handlers), does not report the unchanged voidInvoice action as part of the change, and invents no finding the code does not support (for example no claimed SQL injection, no missing CSRF protection on server actions, no claim that requireSession is missing from bulkDelete)
The review states that lint, typecheck, tests and build were not run (no node_modules, no network), or reports their real output if it ran them; it does not claim the branch builds or passes tests
No file written contains an em dash character
